provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
In original coordinates the generator draws a 9-wide grid. Background-only rows split it into bands of 2x2 blocks: A at x=0-1, B at x=3-4 and C at x=7-8. B is one of three operations applied to A: R (clockwise), L (counter-clockwise) or O (left-right mirror). The fourth option, C, applies a global colour map. The output is the same operation applied to C, written in a 2-wide strip.

The factory tracks where the original x axis lands under the D4 transform. It does this by moving the unit vector (0,+1): it is negated by the row reversal and then rotated (dr,dc)->(dc,-dr) once per clockwise turn. That tells the program three things: whether the A/B/C strips are visible column groups or row groups, whether A sits at the low-index or high-index end, and which strip is C. The background colour is palette[0].

The emitted program works only in visible coordinates. It finds the non-background line groups along both axes. It takes A, B and C directly from the visible pixels and writes each band's result into an output that has the C strip's extent and keeps the visible separators as background.

Transforms are tested on the visible blocks. Conjugating the family operations by the D4 element gives: CW and CCW stay as a pair (reflections swap them), and the left-right mirror becomes an up-down mirror when the number of rotations is odd. The search order is identity, the conjugated family mirror, CW, CCW, then the other symmetries. Only if no pure symmetry fits does it try each symmetry combined with a consistent A->B colour map, identity first. This matches the archived solver's order in the original frame and is equivariant under D4.

In this family a pure symmetry never fits a colour-map band. The generator forbids the map being a swap of the two colours, so B always holds a colour that A lacks. The left-right mirror never fits an R or L band, and CW and CCW never both fit. For R and L bands, C is an injective recolouring of A, so any symmetry that fits gives the same answer. Every colour on C in a colour band appears in A, so the map always covers it.
draft_notes.limitations:
Constructor ambiguity (needs host review): in an O band, A has a single odd cell, so the A->B pair alone is often matched by a rotation as well as the mirror. C's odd cell is placed independently, so the two candidates can give different answers. The visible pair does not settle this; the family prior (mirror before rotations, as in the archived solver) does, and the factory reproduces it through the D4-conjugated mirror axis.

Assumptions:
- Block colours never equal the background, i.e. common.random_colors excludes 0 and the palette is a bijection.
- There are exactly three strip groups. B is taken as the strip next to A.

Demonstrations are not used, because the per-band analogy in the query fully determines the answer. The fixtures are consistent with the rule; I found no contradictions.
draft_notes.host_review: Keep native generator/direct factory unchanged. Independently parse A/B/C bands and enumerate all D4 transformations consistent with A-to-B. Compare all40320 global operation priorities separately for pure-symmetry and symmetry-plus-colour-map stages; demos constrain priorities, query surviving band outputs must agree. Pure geometry is tried before recolouring as the stated family structure; no claim of excluding alternatives beyond that two-stage family. Includes secondary recolour-priority ambiguity. Opposing odd-cell mirror/rotation hypotheses and colour-map hypotheses recover with teaching examples; inconsistent labels and altered separator cells rejected. No hidden prior fallback is accepted by the gate.
